design_summary.purpose: FPGA-friendly single-module PWM LED demo for board prototyping and bring-up, producing a visible breathing/fading LED pattern on a single output using only the board clock and synthesizable RTL suitable for Lattice open-source flows.
design_summary.operating_model: On each rising edge of clk, an 8-bit PWM counter free-runs and is compared against an 8-bit duty-cycle register to drive led. A slow counter or divider generates periodic update events that adjust the duty-cycle register upward or downward under control of a direction bit. When the duty cycle reaches an upper bound, the direction reverses and the duty cycle decreases; when it reaches a lower bound, the direction reverses and the duty cycle increases. The result is a continuously repeating visible breathing effect at a rate intended to be slow and smooth on typical FPGA boards.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.intent: Single synchronous board clock input for all state updates and PWM generation.

external_interfaces.name: led
external_interfaces.intent: Single LED output driven by PWM compare logic; assumed active-high unless external board details indicate otherwise.

module_architecture.name: pwm_fpga_demo
module_architecture.role: Top-level RTL block and only module in this specification scope.
responsibilities: Generate a visible LED breathing/fading PWM pattern from a single board clock input.
Implement an 8-bit PWM compare path for brightness control.
Implement a slow counter or divider to pace duty-cycle updates.
Maintain an 8-bit duty-cycle register that ramps up and down over time.
Maintain a direction bit that controls whether the ramp is increasing or decreasing.
Keep the RTL simple, synthesizable, and compatible with open-source Lattice FPGA flows.
interface_notes: Receives only clk as the clocking input.
Drives only led as the functional output.
Does not expose reset, board-configuration, programming-interface, memory, or vendor-specific ports.
Starter pin constraints are external to the RTL and are not part of the module interface.
ownership_notes: Owns the full breathing PWM behavior within a single synchronous clock domain.
Owns the internal free-running PWM counter, slow timing mechanism, duty-cycle state, and direction state.
Does not own board-specific pin constraints, which must be provided separately after board selection using PCF for iCE40 or LPF for ECP5.

data_flow_summary: clk advances the 8-bit PWM counter continuously, creating the high-frequency carrier used for visible dimming.
The PWM counter is compared against the 8-bit duty-cycle register to determine the instantaneous led output state.
A slow counter or divider generates a much slower terminal event or tick than the PWM carrier.
On each slow update event, the duty-cycle register is incremented or decremented according to the direction bit.
When the duty-cycle register reaches the configured upper limit, the direction bit reverses to decreasing.
When the duty-cycle register reaches the configured lower limit, the direction bit reverses to increasing.
The continuous interaction of PWM compare logic and slow duty-cycle updates creates the breathing/fading brightness pattern.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain driven by clk at the board clock rate specified in the source contract. All sequential state is updated on rising edges of clk. No additional clock domains are introduced.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: No explicit reset input is required. State is expected to rely on synthesizable power-up initialization or inferred initial values where supported by the target FPGA flow, with deterministic startup from a low duty cycle and an initial direction that ramps upward first if initialization is required.

integration_notes: Board-specific starter pin constraints must be generated only after the target board is selected.
Use PCF constraints for iCE40 boards and LPF constraints for ECP5 boards.
Starter constraints are for demo bring-up only and must be reviewed before programming physical hardware.
The RTL must remain portable across Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, timing review, and bitstream handoff workflows.
No ASIC-only constructs, delays, real-number types, DPI, memories, vendor primitives, or testbench-only code are part of the top module contract.
